description:
We are developing MFIEC-AI, an experimental framework for studying adaptation, resilience, recovery, and Effective Contribution in complex systems.

Our project explores how dynamic systems reorganize over time and how key variables contribute to stability and recovery beyond traditional correlation analysis.

We are looking for collaborators interested in AI, data analysis, statistics, software development, space research, and human health monitoring.
summary:
MFIEC-AI is an experimental research framework designed to investigate adaptation, resilience, recovery, and structural reorganization in complex systems.

The project explores how variables contribute to system adaptation beyond traditional correlation-based analysis. Instead of focusing only on statistical relationships, MFIEC-AI analyzes dynamic state transitions, temporal continuity, and reorganization processes to identify potential effective contributors to change.

For the NASA Space Apps Challenge, the framework is applied to astronaut health monitoring, where adaptation, recovery, and stability are critical in long-duration space missions.

The project aims to provide a complementary analytical perspective for understanding how complex systems maintain functionality, recover from disturbances, and adapt under changing conditions.
details:
MFIEC-AI is an experimental framework designed to investigate adaptation, resilience, recovery, and structural reorganization in complex systems.

The project introduces the concept of Effective Contribution Analysis, which seeks to distinguish variables that may actively contribute to adaptation and recovery from variables that merely exhibit statistical correlation with observed outcomes.

The framework combines dynamic state representation, temporal monitoring, reorganization analysis, and Effective Contribution Assessment (ECM). Instead of analyzing isolated observations, MFIEC-AI evaluates how system states evolve over time and how specific factors participate in transitions associated with stability, recovery, and adaptation.

As a proof of concept, the project uses computational models, Python-based analytical pipelines, and publicly available scientific datasets. The initial application focuses on astronaut health monitoring and adaptation during long-duration space missions.

The expected impact is to provide a complementary analytical perspective for studying complex systems in aerospace, environmental science, and technology. The project emphasizes dynamic behavior, temporal continuity, and adaptive processes, offering a framework that may support future research on resilience and system stability under changing conditions.
